steps.a: Synchronizing doesn't help, so it isn't only cross-thread. Looking at who calls `evict`.

Root cause: `StaleRouteListener.onRefreshed` is called synchronously from inside the `routes.values()` loop in `RouteCache.refreshAll`, and it calls `evict`, which removes from the same HashMap on the same thread. The iterator's modCount check then throws ConcurrentModificationException on the next `next()`. It only happens when a refreshed route is expired, which explains the few-per-day rate. A lock can't fix a same-thread modification, which is why synchronizedMap failed. Options for the team: (1) iterate over a snapshot `new ArrayList<>(routes.values())`; (2) collect expired ids and evict after the loop; (3) switch to ConcurrentHashMap, whose weakly consistent iterators tolerate removal, which also covers the admin endpoint's cross-thread `evict`. I haven't changed any code.

reference.summary: Investigated an intermittent ConcurrentModificationException in a scheduled Java job. A listener called during the route cache's map iteration evicts entries from the same map on the same thread; an experiment with a synchronized map still failed, confirming it is not a locking problem. Ended at diagnosis with fix options and no code changed, as requested.
